snapshots.name: Rosalind
snapshots.body: Daughter of the banished Duke Senior, living at the usurping Duke Frederick's court until she too is banished. She flees to the Forest of Arden disguised as a young man, Ganymede.

snapshots.name: Orlando
snapshots.body: The youngest son of the late Sir Rowland de Boys, kept from his inheritance and education by his elder brother Oliver. He falls for Rosalind at a wrestling match before he too is driven to flee to the forest.

snapshots.name: Celia
snapshots.body: Daughter of Duke Frederick and Rosalind's closest companion since childhood. She chooses exile with her cousin rather than remain at her father's court, disguising herself as a shepherdess named Aliena.

snapshots.name: Jaques
snapshots.body: A melancholy lord attending the banished Duke Senior in the forest, given to long, cynical reflections on the world he has left behind. His speeches on life's stages are among the play's most quoted passages.

snapshots.name: Touchstone
snapshots.body: The court fool, who follows Rosalind and Celia into their forest exile. His sharp wit provides a running commentary on the pastoral romance unfolding around him.

snapshots.name: Oliver
snapshots.body: Orlando's elder brother, who has denied him his rightful education and inheritance since their father's death. His mistreatment of Orlando sets the play's opening conflict in motion.

snapshots.name: Duke Frederick
snapshots.body: Usurper of his brother's dukedom, ruling in his place while the rightful duke lives in exile in the forest. His sudden banishment of Rosalind sets much of the play's action moving.

snapshots.name: Duke Senior
snapshots.body: The rightful duke, driven from his position by his own brother and now living contentedly in exile in the Forest of Arden. He has gathered a small court of loyal followers around him there.

snapshots.name: Adam
snapshots.body: An old and faithful servant of the de Boys family, who warns Orlando of danger at his brother's hands and chooses to follow him into exile. His loyalty is offered freely despite his advanced age.

snapshots.name: Silvius
snapshots.body: A young shepherd hopelessly in love with the disdainful Phebe. His earnest, unreturned devotion is played partly for comedy and partly for genuine pathos.

snapshots.name: Phebe
snapshots.body: A proud shepherdess who spurns Silvius's devotion, only to fall for Rosalind in her disguise as the young man Ganymede. Her scorn for one suitor and infatuation with another drive one of the play's comic subplots.

snapshots.name: Audrey
snapshots.body: A simple country goatherd who becomes the object of Touchstone's rather cynical courtship. Their mismatched pairing is one of the play's broader comic threads.

snapshots.name: William
snapshots.body: A country fellow with a claim on Audrey's affections before Touchstone arrives on the scene. His brief encounter with the fool is played for comedy at his expense.

snapshots.name: Corin
snapshots.body: An old shepherd of the forest who offers Rosalind and Celia, arriving as strangers, food and shelter. His practical, unromantic view of country life offers a contrast to the exiles' pastoral idealism.

snapshots.name: Amiens
snapshots.body: A lord attending Duke Senior in his forest exile, known for his singing. His songs help set the pastoral mood of the exiled court.

snapshots.name: Le Beau
snapshots.body: A courtier at Duke Frederick's court who reports the news of the wrestling match to Orlando and Rosalind. His fussy manner is gently mocked by those he addresses.

snapshots.name: Charles
snapshots.body: A professional wrestler in Duke Frederick's service, matched against Orlando at the play's opening. His defeat is the occasion that first brings Orlando to Rosalind's attention.
